baseline.note: The score is a same-day directional release baseline, not a ranking prediction or a production result for the local changes.

criticalFixes.liveFinding: Anonymous mobile article visits could receive a focus-trapped full-screen membership dialog after 3.2 seconds, interrupting reading and locking body scroll.
criticalFixes.localOutcome: Anonymous article visits no longer schedule a wall-clock account offer. The same benefits remain in a non-blocking after-article invitation; the app-level dialog remains only for signed-in preference completion.
invariants: No anonymous account offer is opened by elapsed wall-clock time.
Anonymous article reading never locks body scroll for membership promotion.
Create account, Sign in, and Not now remain together in the after-article invitation.
Signed-in preference completion retains its accessible dialog and focus management.

criticalFixes.liveFinding: Stale Firestore topic overlays could rename a valid server route and canonicalize it to an undeclared direct-request 404; title intent could also diverge after hydration.
criticalFixes.localOutcome: Every code-defined topic retains its canonical slug, eyebrow, title, description, summary, matching terms, short label, required resources, and published state. Custom CMS topics and non-identity presentation fields remain manageable.
invariants: Direct HTTP route, sitemap path, canonical, hydrated URL, H1, title intent, and short label describe one topic.
A stale Firestore record cannot rename or archive a code-defined public topic.
An undeclared alias cannot inherit an indexable topic canonical after hydration.
A future public topic rename requires an explicit redirect, sitemap, canonical, and content migration in one release.

criticalFixes.liveFinding: The physical homepage and 39 other sitemap routes lacked meaningful initial HTML, weakening no-JavaScript access and crawler understanding.
criticalFixes.localOutcome: The physical homepage has a semantic creator fallback, while the catch-all Function renders route-specific article, archive, topic, resource, trust, author, search, and not-found output with appropriate structured data.
invariants: A sitemap route never returns an empty initial app root.
Initial canonical, robots, H1, description, and JSON-LD agree with the requested route.
Unknown, protected, preview, and error routes do not inherit indexable homepage fallback content.
Hosting and all crawler-facing Functions retain the same report-only security-header policy.

deploymentScope.reason: Hosting owns hydrated behavior and physical assets; Functions own initial HTML, sitemap, and feed identity. Shipping only one side can recreate crawler/client drift.

preDeployGates: Review the complete worktree and create one intentional release commit; do not deploy from a dirty tree.
Re-run the focused Angular and Functions suites, Functions build, SEO-shell check, Angular build, lint, and diff check on the exact release commit.
Inspect authenticated CMS Production Preview and sign-in flows because anonymous tests cannot prove protected behavior.
Record current Hosting release and the deployed revisions for renderSeoHtml, sitemapXml, rssFeed, and jsonFeed as rollback authorities.
Obtain explicit approval for the public Hosting and Functions deployment.
postDeployProof: Verify the exact deployed source commit and successful Hosting/Functions deployment state.
Request every sitemap URL and record status, canonical, robots, initial H1, substantive word count, and JSON-LD coverage.
Verify all six topic routes before and after hydration at desktop and 390x844 mobile widths; URL, canonical, H1, and title intent must remain stable.
Verify /topics/weekly-updates returns a true non-indexable 404 and never rewrites a canonical topic.
Use a brand-new browser storage profile to keep an anonymous article open for at least 10 seconds; prove no membership dialog, body lock, horizontal overflow, or blocked reading interaction.
Verify homepage and Temu article console state, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion behavior, and production analytics receipt without sending account or content text.

rollback.hosting: Restore the recorded previous Hosting release.
rollback.functions: Restore the recorded previous revisions for all four crawler-facing Functions.
rollback.firestore: Do not delete or rewrite topic documents; the public identity lock is code-only and custom presentation data remains compatible.
rollback.measurement: Annotate the rollback time so crawler, GA4, and Search Console comparisons do not mix release states.

readiness.reason: The critical fixes pass focused local tests, but the worktree is dirty, no exact release commit exists, authenticated preview is incomplete, and no public deployment approval has been given.
